label: Ptarmigan & Willow
prompt: Refine ONLY this same original Rimebranch Tundra ptarmigan material study. Keep the whole calm familiar ptarmigan bird, exactly two feet, small round eye/short beak, short broad tail and separate three-leaf willow sprig, the coherent pose, pure transparent alpha and clear exterior margins. The first image looks too much like a normal feathered bird with white fern-shaped icing on its feathers. Make the actual body and willow unmistakably a dry grown ICE CRYSTAL sculpture: show angular interlocking straight hexagonal hoarfrost needles and open miniature fern-branched crystal fans with bare rigid blue-clear prismatic edges and frosty opaque cores. Individual icy clusters are broad enough to read at small size, not fuzzy hair or repeating flat fern-leaf stamps. The folded wing is defined by short interlocked branching crystal clusters, not real feather layers. A few clearly straight faceted crystal tips break the contour while the entire bird remains smooth and recognizable overall. Cool white, gray and subtle pale-blue crystalline macro relief with tiny controlled ice highlights; no fur, cloth, feathers, foliage covering a bird, glitter, blue halo, fog, snow ground, glass sphere, paper, ceramic or background. Keep every crystalline tip and leaf whole, central two-thirds composition, soft controlled macro studio light. Transparent background.
processing: Exact original RGBA bytes; whole source retained with no crop, recolour, alpha cleanup or raster art manipulation. App Fit adds its own padding.

references.purpose: Own initial ptarmigan preserves anatomy/pose while correcting a fluffy feather material reading.
